slides: Let's continue with motion, and look at the units.

slides.say: Motion questions love to mix units. So before we calculate, the units must match.

slides: If the speed is in kilometers per hour, the distance must be in kilometers, and the time in hours.

slides.say: One kilometer is a thousand meters.
at: One kilometer is a thousand meters

slides.say: One hour is sixty minutes, and one minute is sixty seconds. So meters per second means how many meters we cover in one second.

slides: Now the most common case. The speed is per hour, but the time is in minutes. So we turn the minutes into part of an hour.

slides.say: Thirty minutes is thirty out of sixty. That's half an hour.
at: Thirty minutes is thirty out of sixty

slides.say: Twenty minutes is twenty out of sixty. We divide both by twenty, and that's one third of an hour.
at: Twenty minutes is twenty out of sixty

slides.say: In the same way, twelve minutes is a fifth of an hour, and fifteen minutes is a quarter. Forty minutes is two thirds, and forty-five minutes is three quarters.
Take a moment to learn this row by heart. It comes up in almost every motion question.
Now a new example. A car drives at sixty kilometers per hour, for forty minutes. How far does it go?
at: A car drives at sixty kilometers per hour

slides.say: The speed is per hour, so the time must be in hours too. Forty minutes is two thirds of an hour.
at: Forty minutes is two thirds of an hour

slides.say: The distance is the speed times the time, so sixty times two thirds. Sixty divided by three is twenty.
at: Sixty divided by three is twenty

slides.say: Then twenty times two is forty. So the car goes forty kilometers.
A lot of students write sixty times forty. That mixes hours with minutes, so the answer is far too big.
Careful with decimals of an hour too. One point two five hours is one hour and a quarter of an hour.
at: One point two five hours is one hour and a quarter

slides.say: A quarter of an hour is fifteen minutes. So one point two five hours is one hour and fifteen minutes, not one hour and twenty-five.
at: So one point two five hours is one hour and fifteen

slides.say: Sometimes we need to change the units of a speed. Some books teach a rule. To go from meters per second to kilometers per hour, multiply by three point six.
You can forget that rule. It almost never comes up on the exam, and almost nobody remembers whether to multiply or to divide.

slides: Instead, we use identical ratios, like in topic twenty-two. If we multiply the time by some number, the distance is multiplied by the same number.

slides.say: Now a new example. A car drives at ninety kilometers per hour. How far does it go in twenty minutes?
at: A car drives at ninety kilometers per hour

slides.say: One hour is sixty minutes. So the car goes ninety kilometers in sixty minutes.
at: So the car goes ninety kilometers
So the car goes ninety kilometers

slides.say: We want twenty minutes. From sixty minutes to twenty minutes, we divide by three.
So we divide the distance by three too. Ninety divided by three is thirty. So in twenty minutes the car goes thirty kilometers.
at: Ninety divided by three is thirty

slides.say: Now the other way. A runner runs ten meters every second. What is his speed in kilometers per hour?
at: A runner runs ten meters every second

slides.say: We write ten meters in one second. Then we grow the time, one step at a time.
at: We write ten meters in one second
We write ten meters in one second

slides.say: From one second to one minute, the time is times sixty, because a minute is sixty seconds.
at: From one second to one minute

slides.say: So the distance is times sixty too. Ten times sixty is six hundred meters in one minute.
at: Ten times sixty is six hundred
six hundred meters in one minute

slides.say: From one minute to one hour, the time is times sixty again.
at: From one minute to one hour

slides.say: So six hundred times sixty. Six hundred times six is three thousand six hundred. So six hundred times sixty is thirty-six thousand meters in one hour.
at: Six hundred times six is three thousand
So six hundred times sixty is thirty-six thousand
thirty-six thousand meters in one hour

slides.say: A thousand meters is one kilometer, so thirty-six thousand meters is thirty-six kilometers.
at: thirty-six thousand meters is thirty-six kilometers

slides.say: So his speed is thirty-six kilometers per hour.

slides: So when a speed comes in other units, don't look for a rule. Change the time step by step, and change the distance in the same way. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
